author: golden state today
title: Cal women's lacrosse faces ranked Duke after close loss to UC Davis
text:
California will travel to Durham to face No. 23 Duke in women’s lacrosse on February 28, marking the third meeting between the programs. Duke leads the all-time series 2-0, including a 13-4 win last season when Cal kept it close at halftime before the Blue Devils pulled away. All four of Cal’s goal scorers from that game—Annette Ciupek, Ashleigh Masterson, Emily Moes and Courtney Wong—remain starters this year.
Cal comes off a narrow 13-12 home loss to UC Davis on February 23. The Golden Bears led by two early in the fourth quarter after Maddie Willkomm scored her fourth goal but could not hold off a late rally by the Aggies, who scored three unanswered goals, capped by Lauren Picardi’s game-winner with just over a minute left.
With three wins in their first five games this season, Cal is seeking its best six-game start since 2018 if it defeats Duke. The team has seen success outside of conference play with an 8-3 nonconference record since joining the Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) before the 2025 campaign.
The upcoming stretch will be challenging for Cal as they are set to play seven teams currently ranked in the IWLCA Division I Coaches Poll over their final twelve regular-season games. This includes matchups against No. 12 Syracuse, No. 11 Boston College, reigning national champion No. 1 North Carolina, and others who participated in last year’s NCAA Championship tournament.
Cal earned its first-ever ACC win earlier this month with a narrow victory over Florida State at home and has played several close games so far this season—three decided by just one goal.
Courtney Wong leads Cal offensively with ten goals and thirteen assists for twenty-three points through five games. Emily Moes follows with twelve goals and four assists while Josie Lillquist adds nine goals and three assists; together they account for more than half of Cal’s scoring output so far.
The team has fielded the same starting lineup throughout these opening contests—a group that includes freshman goalkeeper Lulu Murphy. Murphy is notable as Cal’s first primary freshman starter in net since Jenny Wilkens in 2016 and ranks second among freshmen nationally with thirty-seven saves across five games.
Defensively, Cal is allowing fewer goals per game than last season—down to an average of eleven-point-eight from fourteen—and held opponents under double digits twice during back-to-back wins earlier this month.
Head coach Jennifer Wong is now in her fourth season leading California lacrosse and has improved the team’s record each year since her arrival from Temple University: “Wong is the only head coach in Cal lacrosse history to have won the season-opener in each of her first four campaigns.”
Saturday’s weather forecast for Durham predicts mostly sunny skies with temperatures around sixty-six degrees at game time.
Sophomore Ardyn Henry returns to North Carolina for Saturday’s contest; she played high school lacrosse in Charlotte where she won four state titles at Charlotte Latin School and received multiple All-State honors.
